Paver Driveways in Poinciana, FL

Published 2026-09-11 · By the Kissimmee Concrete team

Poinciana · Osceola / Polk County

The short version for Poinciana

A paver driveway in Poinciana runs $14.00–$22.00 per sq ft (Q3 2026 Cost Index) plus $2 to $4 per square foot to remove the old concrete. The APV Design Control Board lists brick pavers among accepted driveway materials and requires written approval before work starts; on the Osceola side the county driveway permit applies, and on the Polk side pavers that reach the right-of-way need a recorded Paver Release Form. Solivita reviews paver conversions through its own ARC.

Pavers in the villages

Most Poinciana driveways are concrete and most replacements stay concrete, but owners in Villages 7 through 9 and along the Poinciana Parkway side increasingly choose pavers for the look and because a sunken area can be lifted later. Our section is the standard 6 inches of compacted limerock, 1 inch of bedding sand, 80 mm pavers, restraint on the base and polymeric sand; on the Osceola villages' Smyrna and Myakka sand the subgrade is proof-rolled and drained, on the western villages' Candler sand it is wetted before compaction (Paver Base on Flatwoods Sand vs. Ridge Sand: Osceola and Polk Are Not the Same). The apron in the right-of-way is concrete in most cases, with a soldier course at the seam.

DCB, Solivita, and two counties

DCB application first: material, color, pattern, site plan, at 401 Walnut Street (863-427-0900); 30 days of silence is a denial. Solivita residents use the Solivita ARC, which requires replacement driveways in the original builder's style and materials and reviews extensions and modifications, so a concrete-to-paver conversion there is a case-by-case request with a sample. County: Osceola driveway permit under §22-50.6 with the 24-foot limit, or Polk's rules with the notarized, recorded Concrete Driveway Paver Release Form if pavers reach the right-of-way. Pages: Association of Poinciana Villages (APV), Solivita, Unincorporated Osceola County, Polk County (unincorporated), Permit & Jurisdiction Finder.

Worked example

A Village 7 concrete-to-paver conversion

440-square-foot two-car drive, 2004 concrete cracked, Polk side. DCB approval, Polk right-of-way rule handled with a concrete apron so no release form was needed, removal ($880 to $1,760), 6-inch base on wetted Candler sand, 80 mm pavers in herringbone with a soldier border at $14 to $22 ($6,160 to $9,680), seal at 60 days. Four days. Ranges from the Q3 2026 index.

Can I have a paver driveway in Solivita?

Only through the Solivita ARC, and only if it approves a departure from the builder's original material: the requirements say replacement driveways and walkways must be in the same style and material the original builder used, and extensions or modifications are reviewed individually. Some requests are approved with samples; plan on the review before ordering pavers.

Approval

Pavers are an approved material, with conditions

The Design Control Board criteria name brick pavers among the acceptable driveway materials, which makes a paver driveway straightforward to approve in principle. The conditions are where attention is needed. Pavers have to sit flush with the connecting driveway, walkway or roadway, so the transition at the street and at the garage cannot have a lip. Any walkway adjacent to the dwelling is limited to two feet in width unless the board approves otherwise. And approval has to be in hand before work starts.

The flush requirement is a real constraint on a replacement, because eighty millimetre pavers plus a one inch bedding course plus six inches of base is thicker than the four inch slab coming out. Either we excavate deeper, which is normal, or the finished surface sits proud of the street. We excavate.

Base depth on a lot with a fifty-year-old drive

Replacing a 1970s concrete driveway with pavers in Villages 1 through 6 means removing the slab, and what is underneath is not a base. It is the original sand with whatever the last fifty years of roof water has done to it, usually including a washed channel along one edge. That material has to come out to full depth, soft pockets have to be replaced with structural fill compacted in lifts, and then the six inches of limerock goes in.

Contractors who price a paver driveway off the square footage alone and assume they can screed sand over the existing grade produce a field that settles within two wet seasons. Our proposals separate the removal, the fill and the base so the comparison with another quote is on the same terms; the project brief tool produces a specification you can hand to everyone bidding.

On this job

The flush requirement in practice

The Design Control Board criteria require pavers to finish flush with the connecting driveway, walkway or roadway. On a replacement that is a construction requirement rather than a finishing detail, because eighty millimetre pavers on an inch of bedding sand over six inches of base is a thicker build-up than the four-inch slab coming out.

The consequence is deeper excavation and more spoil to haul, which is a real line in the quote rather than an oversight. A paver driveway installed at the existing grade without that excavation sits proud of the street, creates a lip at the garage and at the road, and does not meet the criterion. It is one of the more common reasons a paver job in Poinciana fails inspection by the board rather than by the county.

Questions we get about this

Are pavers allowed by the DCB?

Brick pavers are an accepted driveway material under Criteria 9.1.1, with prior written approval.

What is the Polk Paver Release Form?

A notarized, recorded form the county requires when pavers go in its right-of-way; a concrete apron avoids it.

Concrete or pavers?

Concrete costs less and is the DCB default; pavers can be lifted for repair and widened with matching units.

How long does it take?

Three to five days after DCB approval and the county permit.

Are pavers allowed in Poinciana?

Yes. The published Design Control Board criteria name brick pavers among the acceptable driveway materials, with the condition that they finish flush with the connecting driveway, walkway or roadway.

Why does a paver driveway need deeper excavation than the old slab?

Because eighty millimetre pavers on a one inch bedding course over six inches of base is thicker than the four inch slab being removed, and the finished surface has to stay flush with the street.
